answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy must require real reputation capital to be staked before any vote counts; a newcomer's first block of trust rides on one small deposit rather than a forest of fake identities. The cost curve is like a karst landscape where every cheap clone still drains through the same narrow sinkhole of verification, and over time honest work accumulates into an ocean of attested history that drowns throwaway accounts before they reach a consensus knoll.
